sources.title: The Pyramids and Temples of Gizeh
sources.note: Primary survey of the casing, the passages, and the chambers. Interior positions below are his steel-tape and theodolite figures.

sources.title: Determination of the Exact Size and Orientation of the Great Pyramid of Giza
sources.container: Survey of Egypt Paper No. 39, Government Press, Cairo
sources.note: Invar-wire survey of the casing foot on the pavement. Chosen for the base lengths and the side azimuths.

sources.title: Where in the World Is the Great Pyramid?
sources.container: AERAGRAM, Spring 2018, Ancient Egypt Research Associates
sources.note: WGS84 coordinates of Survey of Egypt station E1 and of the mast on the summit, and the GPMP grid offsets from the base centre.

sources.title: The Great Pyramid's Footprint: Results from Our 2015 Survey
sources.note: Later casing-foot survey. The full corner table is not transcribed in v1; the mean side Dash quotes (755 ft 9 in) is recorded as a candidate.

sources.title: The Complete Pyramids
sources.note: Synthesis of the Giza complex. Cited for the identity of the interior system. Dimensional choices prefer Petrie, Cole, and the muon papers where they give numbers.

sources.authors: Kunihiro Morishima, M. Tayoubi, et al.
sources.title: Discovery of a big void in Khufu's Pyramid by observation of cosmic-ray muons
sources.note: Big Void: at least 30 m long, cross-section similar to the Grand Gallery, above the Grand Gallery, 40–50 m from the Queen's Chamber detectors. No numeric centreline is published.

sources.authors: Sébastien Procureur, Kunihiro Morishima, et al.
sources.title: Precise characterization of a corridor-shaped structure in Khufu's Pyramid by observation of cosmic-ray muons
sources.note: North Face Corridor dimensions and the standing pyramid described as 139 m high and 230 m wide.

sources.authors: Richard William Howard Vyse and John Shae Perring
sources.title: Operations Carried On at the Pyramids of Gizeh in 1837
sources.note: Discovery of the upper relieving chambers. Petrie quotes Vyse for the apex of those chambers near 2,525 inches above the pavement.
